brief:
The Israel lobby has secured substantial influence over American foreign policy through sustained political engagement and strategic organizational efforts, the Quincy Institute reported. The organization examined how pro-Israel advocacy groups have shaped congressional voting patterns, electoral contributions, and executive branch decision-making on Middle East issues over decades.

The Quincy Institute attributed the lobby's reach to its ability to mobilize donors, coordinate messaging across multiple organizations, and cultivate relationships with both major political parties. The institute framed this influence as a significant factor in U.S. policy alignment with Israeli government positions on contentious regional matters.
title: Israel lobby shapes U.S. foreign policy landscape, Quincy Institute argues
